A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-Ensemble research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization and additions.

before.justification: V3 reports original classification, calibration, OOD detection, runtime, and ablation results on CIFAR-10/100, HAM10000, and ESC-50.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds iNaturalist, SST-2, CNN comparisons, and further controlled experiments.

M1.justification: The original transformer procedure—frozen backbone, member-specific low-rank updates, separate classifiers, and prediction averaging—is retained. V4 adds a CNN/ResNet-18 adaptation in Appendix F and introduces the additive Batch-Ensemble++ variant in Appendix G.2; these are localized extensions.

E1.justification: V4 adds large-scale, fine-grained species classification on iNaturalist 2017 and binary sentiment classification on SST-2, substantially extending data scale and task coverage. Existing image, audio, and OOD datasets remain; ESC-50 is relocated to Appendix A.2.

E2.justification: Batch-Ensemble becomes an evaluated comparator on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and HAM10000, whereas v3 only discussed it. V4 also adds Batch-Ensemble++ in Table 13 and a CNN comparison containing MIMO, Masksemble, and FiLM-Ensemble in Table 12; v3's FiLM results concerned a separate ViT experiment.

E3.justification: New protocols include four-member iNaturalist ensembles trained with SGD for 64 epochs, eight-member BERT ensembles on SST-2 with three-epoch training and method-specific learning-rate searches, and four-member ResNet-18 comparisons. V4 also introduces trainable-backbone controls. These are added experimental settings, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E newly tests freezing versus jointly training the backbone, while Appendix G.2 compares multiplicative Batch-Ensemble with additive Batch-Ensemble++. V4 also adds iNaturalist reliability diagrams. The earlier rank, initialization, temperature-scaling, and diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the general five-run, one-sigma reporting practice. V4 introduces an explicit three-seed exception for iNaturalist in Table 4; SST-2 uses five seeds. There is no reported increase in repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Matched earlier scores remain unchanged, while v4 adds baseline rows and substantial new result blocks. For example, Table 4 reports iNaturalist accuracy/ECE of 49.3%/0.045 for LoRA-Ensemble versus 49.6%/0.199 for Explicit Ensemble. These are new results, not version-to-version gains. However, its reported Brier score of 0.160 conflicts with Appendix T.5's definition, which requires at least 0.2535 at 49.3% accuracy; the normalization is unclear.

T1.justification: Appendix G.2 adds gradient-based mathematical reasoning comparing LoRA and Batch-Ensemble, absent from v3. The original update equations and evaluation-metric definitions are retained. This is a localized theoretical addition; the new LoRA gradient expressions in Eqs. 8–9 are dimensionally incomplete as written.

C1.justification: The central contribution and claims of parameter efficiency, competitive accuracy, and improved calibration remain. V4 expands the stated contributions to large-scale fine-grained classification, CNN applicability, and systematic design analyses, while explicitly emphasizing superiority over Batch-Ensemble.

C2.justification: V4 adds hypotheses about backbone training absorbing LoRA adjustments and multiplicative updates coupling ensemble members, alongside explanations involving rank and initialization. It acknowledges weaker CNN performance and removes v3's large-dataset/LLM evaluation caveat. Computational-complexity and finite-ensemble limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 promises a future code and weight release; v4 states that they are released and supplies a repository link. Appendices G and J add Batch-Ensemble forward-pass code and initialization details, plus optimizer, schedule, batch-size, rank, and tuning information for iNaturalist and SST-2. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for BERT, SST-2, GLUE, iNaturalist, Transformers, and a BERT tuning resource, and removes the GPT-3 reference. Positioning against Batch-Ensemble becomes more explicit, but the broader related-work survey and acknowledgment of concurrent LoRA-ensemble research remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, discussion, and conclusion receive substantial editing. Discussion and Related Work exchange order; implementation details and the ESC-50 experiment move into the appendix. V4 also reorganizes appendix headings, adds a contents list, and changes author ordering and contribution markers.

P2.justification: V4 adds five result tables, an iNaturalist reliability figure, and a code listing, and expands existing comparison tables with Batch-Ensemble rows. The original plots are retained, while the schematic is reduced in size and tables and figures are extensively redistributed, including moving ESC-50 results into the appendix.

improvement.justification: Direct Batch-Ensemble comparisons, broader empirical validation, targeted controls, and documented code access strengthen gaps in v3's evidence and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by dimensionally incomplete new gradient formulas and iNaturalist Brier scores inconsistent with the stated definition, limiting the reliability of part of the added mechanistic and calibration evidence.
